availableCommands.name: debug
availableCommands.description: Debug your current Claude Code session by reading the session debug log. (bundled)

availableCommands.name: audit
availableCommands.description: Comprehensive codebase audit for release readiness. Parallel exploration of docs, code, config, tests, and specs to identify cruft, then interactive triage with clear action options. (project)

availableCommands.name: codex
availableCommands.description: Use when the user asks to run Codex CLI (codex exec, codex resume) or wants Codex to review PRs, plans, or specs. Delegates to GPT-5.3-codex with preset reasoning modes. (project)

availableCommands.name: e2e
availableCommands.description: E2E testing patterns for kspec web UI. Use when writing Playwright tests, debugging hydration issues, or working with daemon fixtures. (project)

availableCommands.name: eval-agents
availableCommands.description: Evaluate whether AGENTS.md provides enough context for agents to make correct decisions. Spawns test agents with scenario questions and grades responses. (project)

availableCommands.name: local-review
availableCommands.description: Pre-PR quality review - verify AC coverage, test quality, E2E preference, and test isolation. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr
availableCommands.description: Create a pull request from current work. Handles branch creation, commits, push, and PR creation. Detects branch protection and guides through the PR workflow. (project)

availableCommands.name: pr-review
availableCommands.description: Review a PR linked to a kspec task, post findings as inline comments, and merge only when all quality gates pass. You NEVER fix code — you review and comment. If issues found, kick back to worker. (project)

availableCommands.name: release
availableCommands.description: Create versioned releases - bump version via PR, tag, create GitHub release. CI publishes to npm. (project)

availableCommands.name: svelte-5
availableCommands.description: Svelte 5 patterns, gotchas, and solutions. Use when working with Svelte 5/SvelteKit, especially for reactivity, SSR, and state management issues. (project)

availableCommands.name: create-workflow
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Formalize repeatable patterns into trackable kspec workflows. Design steps, choose triggers, create loop variants, and integrate with skills.

availableCommands.name: help
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Get help with kspec commands and workflows

availableCommands.name: observe
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Capture and act on systemic patterns — friction, successes, questions, and ideas. The feedback loop that drives process improvement.

availableCommands.name: plan
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Translate approved plans into specs and tasks. Import structured documents or create incrementally. Plans persist as durable artifacts with audit trail.

availableCommands.name: reflect
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured reflection at the end of work sessions. Identifies learnings, friction points, and improvements for system evolution.

availableCommands.name: review
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Kspec-specific review gates — spec alignment, own AC coverage, trait AC coverage, and validation integration. Building block for project-specific review workflows.

availableCommands.name: task-work
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Structured task lifecycle — start, work, note, submit, complete. Fix cycle handling, scope management, loop mode for automation, and quality gates.

availableCommands.name: triage
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Triage inbox items systematically. Records decisions with audit trail, then executes actions. Supports inbox, observations, and automation eligibility triage.

availableCommands.name: triage-automation
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Assess and prepare tasks for automation eligibility. Verify spec coverage, acceptance criteria, and task readiness for automated agents.

availableCommands.name: triage-inbox
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Process inbox items using the record-act pattern. Categorize, promote to spec/task, merge duplicates, defer, or delete stale items with full audit trail.

availableCommands.name: writing-specs
availableCommands.description: (kspec) Create and maintain specification items — modules, features, requirements, acceptance criteria, and traits. The source of truth for what to build.

availableCommands.description: Clear conversation history but keep a summary in context. Optional: /compact [instructions for summarization]

Type: feature

  New kspec agent command family for managing and running agents.

Acceptance Criteria:
  [ac-1]
    Given: Agent definitions exist in meta

    When: kspec agent list is run

    Then: All agent definitions are listed with id, adapter, dispatch

  [ac-2]
    Given: An agent definition exists with id "worker"

    When: kspec agent run worker --task @task-ref is run

    Then: A one-shot invocation is created using the agent's adapter and
configuration, targeted at the specified task, with a full
session created and logged

  [ac-3]
    Given: An agent definition exists

    When: kspec agent run <name> "custom prompt text" is run without --task

    Then: A one-shot invocation is created with the provided prompt and
no task binding in the session metadata

  [ac-4]
    Given: The daemon is running

    When: kspec agent dispatch start is run

    Then: The dispatch engine begins watching for state changes and
dispatching agents per their rules

  [ac-5]
    Given: The dispatch engine is running

    When: kspec agent dispatch stop is run

    Then: The dispatch engine stops accepting new triggers, waits for
active invocations to complete, then shuts down

  [ac-6]
    Given: Agent invocations are running or queued

    When: kspec agent status is run

    Then: Active invocations and queued invocations are displayed with
session IDs, agent names, task refs, and elapsed time

  [ac-7]
    Given: kspec agent run is used with --budget, --timeout, or --adapter

    When: These flags differ from the agent definition defaults

    Then: The invocation uses the CLI-specified values, overriding the
definition defaults for this invocation only

  [ac-8]
    Given: kspec agent run is used with --dry-run

    When: The command is executed

    Then: The prompt that would be sent is displayed without spawning
the agent process

  [ac-9]
    Given: kspec agent dispatch status is run

    When: The daemon is running

    Then: Shows whether dispatch is enabled, number of active and queued
invocations, and loaded agent definitions

  [ac-10]
    Given: The daemon is not running

    When: kspec agent dispatch start is run

    Then: An error message explains that the daemon must be running and
suggests kspec serve to start it

  [ac-11]
    Given: kspec agent run completes with --json flag
    When: the invocation produces text output
    Then: streaming output is suppressed; the JSON result object includes outcome, session_id, duration_ms, and stop_reason only
  [ac-12]
    Given: kspec agent run is used in interactive mode (not --json)
    When: the agent produces text output during the invocation
    Then: text content streams to stdout as it is received, so the user sees the response live without waiting for completion
  [ac-13]
    Given: kspec agent dispatch watch is run while the daemon has active or future agent invocations
    When: An agent produces text output
    Then: Text output streams to stdout in real time with [agent-id session-id] prefixed once per rendered line. Continuation chunks append to the current line, and watch starts a new prefixed line at newline characters, ACP empty-chunk message boundaries, or stream switches. When adapters omit empty-chunk delimiters, watch may also split at conservative sentence boundaries (previous chunk ends with sentence punctuation and next chunk starts a capitalized token).
  [ac-14]
    Given: kspec agent dispatch watch is run
    When: The WebSocket connection to the daemon drops
    Then: The command automatically attempts to reconnect and prints a reconnecting message; reconnect notices are emitted on their own line (not appended to active agent output), and the command exits with code 3 if reconnection fails after retries.
  [ac-15]
    Given: kspec agent dispatch watch is run
    When: The daemon is not running
    Then: An error message explains the daemon must be running and suggests kspec serve to start it; exits with code 3
  [ac-16]
    Given: kspec agent dispatch watch is run with --agent <name> or --session <id>
    When: Output arrives from multiple concurrent invocations
    Then: Only output matching the specified agent name or session ID is shown; unmatched chunks are silently dropped
  [ac-17]
    Given: kspec agent dispatch watch receives text events containing full session ULIDs
    When: A watch line prefix is rendered
    Then: The session component in [agent-id session-id] uses the first 8 characters of the session ULID for readability.

[2026-03-04T03:54:31.872Z] Jacob Chapel:
Posted clean PR review on #657 (GitHub review id 3886542494). No MUST-FIX/SHOULD-FIX findings after AC/spec/code-quality/regression checks. Note: self-approval is disallowed by GitHub for own PR, so clean review was posted as COMMENT. CI checks still pending before merge.
[2026-03-04T04:20:27.521Z] Jacob Chapel:
Follow-up fix after manual watch validation: coalesce tiny token chunks (50ms) so each logical update renders on its own line, flush active line before reconnect messages, and display shortened 8-char session IDs in watch prefixes. Added regressions for same-stream line separation, short session ID display, and reconnect flush behavior. [2026-03-04T04:29:59.330Z] Jacob Chapel:
Aligned dispatch watch rendering to legacy Ralph parser semantics: removed heuristic line splitting, now break lines on explicit boundaries (newline, stream switch, ACP empty chunk sentinel) so message chunks coalesce naturally.
